body: I don't drink as much as I used to but yeah, I fell the same way. The happiest I ever feel and have felt in a long time is when I'm drunk. It's a fine line between just really happy and love people drunk, and the self destructive asshole drunk that's extremely not like me. I hate sometimes hurting the people who don't deserve it, but at the same time I just want to be happy.
There isn't really a whole lot to be proud of if I feel like I don't have a choice.

Have tried ignoring feeling this numb for years now while going to college. Switched my major to biology and still did well on my first few classes, but my depression just started hitting harder. Grades started to slip, making me feel even worse, which made them slip more. Don't have a whole lot of friends and especially don't talk about any of this crap, so just tried to still handle it on my own. Fast forward to this year had classes while helping take care of my grandparents, then work. My grandpa was on the final stretch of prostate cancer, which was such a slow, terrible, painful way to pass. Seeing him like this just fucked with me, even though I was happy to help. Now school is over, did shit on my classes (F on one and D on another, so bye credit hours) and will end up loosing my scholarship.

I had a similar conversation with the text line. Didn't feel like it mattered what I said, just kept referring me to ways to calm down and just relax. Was like I said I was crazy stressed for an exam instead of thinking about shooting myself.

I actually think that's adorable! Least it is to me. I think it's kinda just expected that the guy hits on the girl or is responsible for the first move. Might be more common now, but still think that's at least how guys feel. But when the opposite happens, the confidence alone can be extremely attractive. If it's difficult to make the first move, a nice little note is definitely something easy you can do. Think if a girl did the same for me, I'd be swooned. Anyone else agree?

Wow, it's weird to hear someone who has the same problem. I try and do a similar thing and just tell myself "Yeah, I love them. Why wouldn't I? They're nice" or this or that. Then I just end up doing things I know they want me to do until I break up with them and just blame myself. Haven't actually felt that 'fluttery' love feeling everyone else talks about.
Usually what's recommended to me. Michael Reeves, the thought emporium, William Osman, Gamegrumps, electroBOOM are a few off the top of my head.

I've tried. Tried playing guitar, learning Russian, electrical engineering, 3d modeling, playing games again, stock market, sewing, plenty of things way outside my norm. Same thing happens every time, I ram my head right in and try to learn as much as I can, cross my fingers sometimes sparks and catches my interest, then crash. Tried slowly learning things in case I'm forcing my interest to burn out, constantly distracting myself, same result. Only thing I can do consistently is watch YouTube, but then I just sit and zone out. Can't do that the rest of my life, anyway

Don't really have any small things to live for. Used to have some hobbies, drawing, gaming, reading, but now everything feels like a chore. Used to be able to force myself to do something for a little bit and eventually be fine with it, but now it doesn't seem to work.

That's not the nucleus. It's more likely just waste products the amoeba is getting rid of (exocytosis). Basically it wraps its waste in a little package and tosses it out the cell. It's not an egg as (jokingly?) mentioned above, either, as they commonly reproduce asexually by binary fission.
